'''''Plantago maritima''''', the '''sea plantain''', '''seaside plantain'''  or '''goose tongue''', is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the plantain family [[Plantaginaceae]]. It has a [[cosmopolitan distribution|subcosmopolitan]] distribution in temperate and Arctic regions, native to most of Europe, northwest Africa, northern and central Asia, northern North America, and southern South America.<ref name=grin>{{GRIN | accessdate = 24 December 2017}}</ref><ref name=flora>Flora Europaea: [http://rbg-web2.rbge.org.uk/cgi-bin/nph-readbtree.pl/feout?FAMILY_XREF=&GENUS_XREF=Plantago&SPECIES_XREF=maritima&TAXON_NAME_XREF=&RANK= ''Plantago maritima'']</ref>

==Description==
It is a [[herbaceous]] [[perennial plant]] with a dense [[rosette (botany)|rosette]] of [[leaf|leaves]] without [[Petiole (botany)|petioles]]. Each leaf is linear, {{Convert|2-22|cm|4=1|abbr=on}} long and under {{Convert|1|cm|4=1|abbr=on}} broad, thick and fleshy-textured, with an acute apex and a smooth or distantly toothed margin; there are three to five veins. The [[flower]]s are small, greenish-brown with brown [[stamen]]s, produced in a dense spike {{Convert|0.5-10|cm|4=1|abbr=on}} long on top of a stem {{Convert|3-20|cm|abbr=on}} tall.<ref name=blamey>Blamey, M. & Grey-Wilson, C. (1989). ''Flora of Britain and Northern Europe''. {{ISBN|0-340-40170-2}}</ref><ref name=bc>Plants of British Columbia: [http://linnet.geog.ubc.ca/Atlas/Atlas.aspx?sciname=Plantago+maritima ''Plantago maritima'']</ref><ref name=arctic>Flora of the Canadian Arctic Archipelago: [https://www.mun.ca/biology/delta/arcticf/_ca/www/plplma.htm ''Plantago maritima'']</ref>

===Subspecies===
There are four [[subspecies]]:<ref name=flora/><ref name=arctic/>
*''Plantago maritima'' subsp. ''maritima''. Europe, Asia, northwest Africa.
*''Plantago maritima'' subsp. ''borealis'' (Lange) A. Blytt and O. Dahl. Arctic regions. All parts of the plant small, compared to temperate plants.
*''Plantago maritima'' subsp. ''juncoides'' (Lam.) Hultén. South America, North America (this name to North American plants has been questioned<ref name=arctic/>).
*''Plantago maritima'' subsp. ''serpentina'' (All.) Arcang. Central Europe, on [[serpentine soil]]s in mountains.

===Ecology and physiology===
In much of the range it is strictly [[coast]]al, growing on sandy soils. In some areas, it also occurs in [[alpine plant|alpine]] habitats, along mountain streams.<ref name=blamey/> Some of the physiology and metabolism of this species has been described, of particular note is how the metabolism of this species is altered with elevated atmospheric carbon dioxide concentrations.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Davey | first1 = M. == Uses ==
Like [[samphire]]s, the leaves of the plant are harvested to be eaten raw or cooked.<ref name="PFAF">{{citation|title=Plants for a Future|url=http://www.pfaf.org/User/Plant.aspx?LatinName=Plantago+maritima|access-date=9 November 2016}}</ref><ref>Seymour, Tom, ''Foraging New England:  Edible wild food and medicinal plants from Maine to the Adirondacks to Long Island Sound'', 2nd ed. (Guilford, Connecticut:  Morris Book Publishing, 2013), [https://books.google.com/books?id=JbWCBAAAQBAJ&pg=PA2 pp. 2-4.]  See also:  Seymour, Tom (June 2009), [http://www.fishermensvoice.com/archives/0609freelunch.html "Free Lunch:  Foraging the Maine Seashore,"] ''Fishermen's Voice'' (Gouldsboro, Maine, U.S.).</ref> The seeds are also eaten raw or cooked, and can be ground into flour.<ref name="PFAF" />
